_meta.status: Oct 28 hemorrhage kit from OCT28_MEDICAL_ANSWERS section 5. Typical ALS ambulance layout. Needs sign-off from a certified medic before Nov 4.
_meta.gameplayRule: The jump bag is what is at the patient. Cabinet items require someone to go to the truck: 45-60 s round trip (partner or player).
_meta.oct29Note: Oct 29 adds airway, breathing, lines/fluids, assessment and monitor items from OCT28_MEDICAL_ANSWERS section 7, plus the hypothermia wrap blanket the Oct 28 build used untracked. Oct 29 quantities are logistical placeholders for Wyatt sign-off, not clinical values. Stash rule unchanged: belt + jump_bag are at the patient, cabinet needs a truck fetch.

equipment.name: CAT tourniquet
equipment.notes: Belt 1, jump 2, cabinet 4.

equipment.name: SOF-T Wide tourniquet
equipment.notes: Cabinet only.

equipment.name: Junctional tourniquet (SAM JT)
equipment.notes: Cabinet only. Many civilian units do not carry one; keep it in the cabinet.

equipment.name: Hemostatic gauze, z-fold (Combat Gauze / QuikClot)
equipment.notes: Jump 2, cabinet 4.

equipment.name: Plain gauze roll (Kerlix)
equipment.notes: Jump 4, cabinet 10. Packs at about 75 percent instead of 90.

equipment.name: Pressure bandage 6 in (Israeli / emergency trauma bandage)
equipment.notes: Jump 2, cabinet 6.

equipment.name: Pressure bandage 4 in
equipment.notes: Jump 2, cabinet 4.

equipment.name: Elastic wrap (ACE)
equipment.notes: Jump 2, cabinet 6.

equipment.name: Trauma dressing 10x30
equipment.notes: Jump 2, cabinet 4.

equipment.name: ABD pad
equipment.notes: Jump 6, cabinet 10.

equipment.name: Trauma shears
equipment.notes: Belt 1, jump 1, cabinet 1. Needed to expose the wound.

equipment.name: Vented chest seal
equipment.notes: Jump 2, cabinet 4. Parked use until R step depth lands; carried for inventory truth.

equipment.name: Sharpie (TQ time)
equipment.notes: Belt 1, jump 1. No time written is logged and missing from MIST.

equipment.name: Hypothermia wrap blanket
equipment.notes: Oct 29 fix-up: the Oct 28 wrap action used an untracked blanket. Now tracked. Jump 1, cabinet 2 (placeholder counts).

equipment.name: OPA set (80/90/100 mm)
equipment.notes: Airway bag staged at the patient counts as jump_bag stash. Josh: 100 mm (90 acceptable).

equipment.name: NPA set (26-34 Fr)
equipment.notes: Josh: 30-32 Fr.

equipment.name: i-gel set (#3/#4/#5)
equipment.notes: Josh: #4 (50-90 kg band).

equipment.name: King LT set (#3/#4/#5)
equipment.notes: Josh: #4 (5-6 ft band).

equipment.name: ETT set (6.0-8.5 + laryngoscope + bougie)
equipment.notes: Josh: 7.5-8.0 at 22-23 cm. Waveform EtCO2 is the only reliable confirmation.

equipment.name: BVM adult (1,500 mL bag + large mask)
equipment.notes: Josh mask: large. Deliver 500-600 mL, one breath every 6 s.

equipment.name: Suction unit + rigid Yankauer
equipment.notes: Rigid Yankauer for the mouth. Max 10-15 s per pass.

equipment.name: Suction catheter 14 Fr (for ETT)
equipment.notes: 14 Fr flexible catheter for the ETT.

equipment.name: Waveform EtCO2 module
equipment.notes: The only reliable ETT confirmation. Shows waveform or no waveform.

equipment.name: Nasal cannula
equipment.notes: 1-6 L, 24-44 percent (+4 percent per L).

equipment.name: Simple O2 mask
equipment.notes: 6-10 L, 35-60 percent.

equipment.name: Non-rebreather mask
equipment.notes: 10-15 L, 60-90 percent. Reservoir must be pre-inflated or the patient rebreathes (trap).

equipment.name: CPAP unit
equipment.notes: 5-10 cmH2O. Cabinet only on Oct 29.

equipment.name: O2 D cylinder (2,000 psi full)
equipment.notes: Portable D staged at the patient. Factor 0.16. Full D at 15 L/min is about 19 min. Can run out.

equipment.name: O2 M cylinder (truck)
equipment.notes: Truck M cylinder. Factor 1.56. Fetch to swap when the D runs dry.

equipment.name: IV catheter 14g orange (300 mL/min)
equipment.notes: Gravity flow 300 mL/min crystalloid.

equipment.name: IV catheter 16g gray (200 mL/min)
equipment.notes: Gravity flow 200 mL/min crystalloid.

equipment.name: IV catheter 18g green (100 mL/min)
equipment.notes: Gravity flow 100 mL/min crystalloid.

equipment.name: IV catheter 20g pink (60 mL/min)
equipment.notes: Gravity flow 60 mL/min crystalloid.

equipment.name: IV catheter 22g blue (35 mL/min)
equipment.notes: Gravity flow 35 mL/min crystalloid.

equipment.name: IV catheter 24g yellow (20 mL/min)
equipment.notes: Gravity flow 20 mL/min crystalloid.

equipment.name: EZ-IO drill
equipment.notes: 20-40 s, about 95 percent success.

equipment.name: EZ-IO needle 15 mm (3-39 kg)
equipment.notes: Peds needle. Wrong for Josh.

equipment.name: EZ-IO needle 25 mm (adult tibial)
equipment.notes: Josh tibial needle.

equipment.name: EZ-IO needle 45 mm (humeral or obese)
equipment.notes: Josh humeral needle.

equipment.name: Macro drip set (10/15/20 gtt/mL)
equipment.notes: gtt/min = mL/h x drop factor / 60. Player sets the rate at L4+.

equipment.name: Micro drip set (60 gtt/mL)
equipment.notes: 60 gtt/mL.

equipment.name: Pressure bag (300 mmHg)
equipment.notes: About 1.5-2x gravity flow.

equipment.name: Fluid warmer (38 C)
equipment.notes: Blood products need a warmer at 38 C. Cabinet only.

equipment.name: Blood tubing with filter
equipment.notes: Blood products need blood tubing with a filter. Cabinet only.

equipment.name: Normal saline 1,000 mL bag
equipment.notes: Crystalloid: +1,000 mL intravascular now, about 250 mL retained over 60 min.

equipment.name: Lactated Ringers 1,000 mL bag
equipment.notes: Crystalloid: same explicit decay as saline.

equipment.name: Whole blood unit (cooler)
equipment.notes: Stays about 90 percent intravascular. Needs blood tubing + warmer at 38 C. Cooler on the truck.

equipment.name: Syringe 3 mL
equipment.notes: Drug box staged at the patient. Dose = mL x concentration.

equipment.name: Syringe 10 mL
equipment.notes: Drug box staged at the patient.

equipment.name: Syringe 20 mL
equipment.notes: Drug box staged at the patient.

equipment.name: Stethoscope
equipment.notes: Auscultated BP and lung sounds.

equipment.name: BP cuff adult
equipment.notes: Correct cuff for Josh. Width about 40 percent of arm circumference.

equipment.name: BP cuff large
equipment.notes: Too big for Josh: reads LOW -5-10.

equipment.name: BP cuff peds
equipment.notes: Too small for Josh: reads HIGH +10-30.

equipment.name: Penlight
equipment.notes: Pupil check, each eye plus consensual.

equipment.name: Glucometer + strips
equipment.notes: Fingerstick, +/-15 percent.

equipment.name: Thermometer (tympanic/oral/temporal)
equipment.notes: Temporal reads low in cold or sweaty skin.

equipment.name: Monitor/defib (SpO2 + NIBP + EtCO2)
equipment.notes: Staged at the patient. SpO2 pleth, NIBP auto cycle, EtCO2 waveform. Pacing/cardioversion parked.
